title: Greenpill Phangan: Cleanups and Environmental Monitoring
dek: Greenpill Phangan's work on Koh Phangan runs from beach cleanups to DeCleanup Network and community air quality sensors.
excerpt: A cleanup idea born in the chapter became DeCleanup Network, which added AI-assisted verification and Gardens governance in 2026.
body:
Greenpill Phangan began about a year before its first update on the Regen Coordination Hub in August 2024, with onboarding events called Regen Full Moon, held with ReFi Phangan. The chapter focuses on local regeneration infrastructure and public goods funding on Koh Phangan, Thailand, and started work on a quadratic funding round for island projects.

## From cleanups to DeCleanup Network

The chapter's cleanups began with a simple registration form: participants uploaded a cleanup photo and received an Unlock Protocol certificate. The idea grew into an independent project, the Decentralized Cleanup Network, while the chapter kept running joint beach cleanups with local regens as part of Monthly Earth Day. In October 2024, the chapter's founders introduced DeCleanup Rewards, an app on Arbitrum for turning cleanup photos into an onchain record.

On February 24, 2026, DeCleanup Network reported that its rewards mini app was live on Base, inside Farcaster and the Base app, that its full platform on Celo was in testing, and that its docs and playbook were published. In an update on August 17, 2026, it added AI-assisted verification with automated fraud scoring and waste categorization, opened governance on Gardens, and announced a partnership with Global Cleanup Games on the Trash Athlete Challenge: pick up one piece of trash a day for 30 days.

## Measuring the air

In May 2025, the chapter began placing Altruist air quality sensors from the Robonomics network at around five locations on the island. In July 2025 it published an analysis on the Hub of decentralized environmental monitoring for Koh Phangan, covering gaps in local data, pollution peaks during big tourist events, and the case for community-run sensors.
